# Probabilistic sensitivity analysis -- ciNPWT after instrumented posterior lumbar fusion

> **VERIFIED RESULTS -- Phase A2 full-text verification completed 2026-08-17: 46 of 48 parameters were closed out against the 14 source full texts and 43 carry a table/page locator; 2 remain unresolvable assumptions (the ciNPWT institutional net acquisition price and the superficial tunnel length). SSI/ciNPWT risk-threshold Markov CUA; US commercial payer; 2025 USD; monthly cycles; 24-cycle base horizon; 3%/yr discounting; WTP $100000/QALY.**

*Generated by `run_psa.py` from the read-only engine (`inputs.py` / `model.py`). Model-based result; not a substitute for clinical evidence.*

## What was run

- **10,000 Monte-Carlo iterations**, `np.random.default_rng(12345)`.
- Horizon 24 cycles (2 years); 3%/yr discounting on costs and QALYs; trapezoidal half-cycle correction on dwell streams only; 2025 USD.
- **16 parameters sampled**; 32 excluded, every one of them logged below.
- Distribution fitting: `[low, high]` treated as an approximate 95% CI, `SE = (high - low) / 3.92`, **method of moments preserving the mean** -- except relative effects, sampled on the log scale preserving the **median** (`sdlog = (ln(high) - ln(low)) / 3.92`), so RR stays below 1 in every draw and arm ordering is preserved.
- **Correlation.** The engine applies `p_ciNPWT = p_control x RR` internally, so the two arms are correlated by construction; the RR is never pre-multiplied here.
- **One sample set of 10,000 draws is reused at every risk point** (common random numbers). This is deliberate: for a fixed draw INMB is strictly increasing in `p`, so reusing the draws is what makes the acceptability curve monotone rather than jittery, and it keeps the sweep to a single pass.
- Acceptability-by-risk subgrid: **every 5th point** of the 291-point `SETTINGS['risk_grid']` **plus the three reported strata** (0.066 and 0.114 are not multiples of 5 on that grid) = **61 risk points**, p = 0.0050 to 0.1500, i.e. 610,000 `run_pair` calls. (Wall-clock runtime is printed to stdout and recorded in `run_log.d/run_psa.md`, deliberately **not** written here: it is machine-dependent, and every file in `v2/results/` must be byte-reproducible from the seed.)
- Cost draws are expressed in each parameter's **own stored price year** (the six commercial SSI tranches in 2019 USD, `c_device_cinpwt` in 2025 USD); the engine inflates exactly once. No cost is read with `val()`.

## Headline results, by risk stratum

ciNPWT minus standard dressing, 2-year horizon. **`icer` is NaN wherever ciNPWT is dominant**, which is most of the range at and above the intermediate stratum, so nothing here averages an ICER: the summary is built on INMB and on the cost-effectiveness-plane frequencies.

| stratum | p | inc. cost, mean (95% CrI) | inc. QALY, mean (95% CrI) | INMB @ $100k, mean (95% CrI) |

| low | 0.020 | -$42 (-$304 to $408) | +0.00060 (+0.00029 to +0.00099) | $102 (-$352 to $387) |
| intermediate | 0.066 | -$827 (-$1,354 to -$224) | +0.00199 (+0.00097 to +0.00327) | $1,025 ($353 to $1,635) |

That is not fussiness: at the intermediate stratum P(CE) is 0.9999, and rounding it to `1.000` would assert a certainty the PSA does not have in the same row that reports a draw which is *not* dominant. No probability in this table is exactly 0 or exactly 1.

| low | 0.7070 | 0.7481 | 0.7830 | 0.6592 | 0.0000 | 0.6592 | 1.0000 | 3,408 / 10,000 |

### The PSA means do NOT reproduce the deterministic base case -- and that is a property of the fit, not Monte-Carlo noise

A reviewer holding Table 2 beside this table will find the two INMB columns disagree, in the **same direction at every stratum**: the PSA mean sits 5.59% below the deterministic value at the intermediate stratum ($1,025.11 against $1,085.84), and 34.00% below it at the low stratum, where the same handful of dollars is a much larger share of a much smaller INMB. The gap is 18.6 Monte-Carlo standard errors at the intermediate stratum, so it is **not** noise. The two are different estimands, and the difference is explained here rather than left for a reader to find:

| stratum | p | deterministic INMB @ $100k | PSA mean INMB | gap | MCSE | gap / MCSE | gap % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | 0.020 | $154.80 | $102.17 | -$52.63 | $1.88 | -28.03 | -33.996% |
| intermediate | 0.066 | $1,085.84 | $1,025.11 | -$60.73 | $3.26 | -18.64 | -5.593% |
| high | 0.114 | $2,057.36 | $1,988.17 | -$69.19 | $5.11 | -13.54 | -3.363% |

**The dominant mechanism is the mandated median-preserving lognormal on `rr_cinpwt`.** BUILD-CONTRACT section 9 and the PSA convention require relative effects to be sampled on the log scale preserving the **median**, so the drawn RR has median 0.610403 (theoretical median exactly 0.61) but **mean 0.613982** -- theory 0.61 x exp(0.11197^2 / 2) = 0.613836. The deterministic base case uses 0.61. A **higher mean RR means fewer SSIs averted**, so the mean INMB across draws must sit below the INMB evaluated at the deterministic RR. The two numbers answer different questions: the deterministic value is INMB at the median effect, the PSA value is the mean INMB over the effect distribution. A mean-preserving lognormal would close the gap and was deliberately **not** used -- it would put the median draw off the base case and let RR draws exceed 1.

**A second, smaller term** is the device-price truncation (below): rejection-truncating `c_device_cinpwt` to its $100-$900 axis removes more mass below $100 than above $900, so the mean sampled price is $299.10 against the deterministic $250.00 -- a fixed shift of about $49.10 per patient at every stratum, which is why it dominates the *relative* gap at the low stratum and barely moves it at the high one.

Both are measured, not asserted -- the engine was re-run deterministically at the **mean of the draws** and reproduces the PSA means to within a few dollars:

| stratum | deterministic | + drawn mean RR | + drawn mean device price | PSA mean | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | $154.80 | $150.67 | $101.57 | $102.17 | $0.61 |
| intermediate | $1,085.84 | $1,072.20 | $1,023.10 | $1,025.11 | $2.01 |
| high | $2,057.36 | $2,033.80 | $1,984.70 | $1,988.17 | $3.47 |

The residual -- what is left after the two mean shifts are accounted for -- is a few dollars at every stratum, which is Monte-Carlo noise on the remaining parameters and nonlinearity. **Do not "fix" the gap by re-centring the sampler**: the median-preserving fit is contract-mandated and is what keeps every RR draw below 1. Report the deterministic value as the base case and the PSA mean as the mean over the parameter distribution, and say that they differ for this reason.

## Acceptability by risk -- the novel output (Fig 4)

`acceptability_by_risk.csv` reports P(ciNPWT cost-effective) as a function of the baseline 90-day all-SSI risk `p`, conditioning on `p` rather than integrating over it. The curve is **monotone non-decreasing in `p`** (asserted live at every WTP, not assumed).

| WTP | p at P(CE) = 0.50 | p at P(CE) = 0.80 | p at P(CE) = 0.95 | P(CE) at p = 0.005 | P(CE) at p = 0.150 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $50,000/QALY | 1.40% | 2.41% | 3.82% | 0.019 | 1.000 |
| $100,000/QALY | 1.29% | 2.24% | 3.54% | 0.032 | 1.000 |
| $150,000/QALY | 1.20% | 2.08% | 3.30% | 0.049 | 1.000 |

Read against the deterministic threshold (`run_threshold.py`), this is the probabilistic statement of the same result: the deterministic `p*` is where the *mean* INMB crosses zero, while the value above is where *half the draws* cross it. The gap between the 0.50 and 0.95 crossings is the width of the decision's uncertainty in the units the clinical question is actually asked in -- a patient's predicted risk.

## The three sampling-rule disclosures (BUILD-CONTRACT section 9)

### 1. `p_base_ssi` was never sampled -- it is the x-axis, not an uncertain input

`p_base_ssi` carries `dist='beta'` and a (0.005, 0.15) range, so a generic "sample every non-`fixed` Param" loop would have drawn it. It is excluded **by name**. Every acceptability number above is a probability **conditional on** `p`; integrating over `p` would have collapsed Fig 4 into a single number and silently answered a different question.

### 2. `du_sup` / `du_deep` were truncated at 0 by RESAMPLING (not clipping)

Both are `normal` on a quantity that must be non-negative -- a negative draw is a utility *gain* from surgical-site infection. A normal fitted to (0.08, 0.05, 0.11) has SE 0.0153, so 0 is 5.2 SD away and about 1e-7 of draws go negative. Negative draws were **rejected and redrawn**, not clipped to 0: clipping would pile them onto exactly 0 and create a spurious point mass at "SSI costs no utility at all".

- `du_sup` (mean 0.08, SE 0.015306, so 0 is 5.23 SD away, P(negative draw) = 8.63e-08, expected 0.0009 negative draws in 10,000): **0 rejected and redrawn** at this seed. The guard is active but did not fire -- which is the expected outcome at this SE, not evidence that it is unnecessary: it is what keeps a future A2-revised (wider) decrement from silently producing a utility gain.
- `du_deep` (mean 0.1, SE 0.020408, so 0 is 4.90 SD away, P(negative draw) = 4.79e-07, expected 0.0048 negative draws in 10,000): **0 rejected and redrawn** at this seed. The guard is active but did not fire -- which is the expected outcome at this SE, not evidence that it is unnecessary: it is what keeps a future A2-revised (wider) decrement from silently producing a utility gain.

**The same idiom is applied to `c_device_cinpwt`**, truncated to its declared $100-$900 range rather than at a single bound -- there the guard fires hard (3,535 draws rejected and redrawn). See the fourth disclosure below; it is a decision about the price *axis*, not about non-negativity, so it is reported there rather than here.

### 3. `m_ssi_cost` stayed `fixed` -- the CEAC does NOT carry attribution uncertainty

**State this plainly wherever the CEAC is shown.** SSI-attributable-cost *attribution* is structural between-source disagreement -- Pennington's matched increment against Edmiston's regression-adjusted all-cause increment, a 3.9-fold span (0.306 to 1.199 on `m_ssi_cost`) -- and the contract handles it **deterministically**, through the all-cause x1.000 scenario and through the DSA, where it must be the top tornado bar. It is therefore **not sampled here**. The consequence is that **the CEAC, the acceptability-by-risk curve and Fig 4 are more confident than the evidence supports**: they propagate sampling noise on the six cost tranches while the single largest cost uncertainty in the model is absent. A reader who sees the tornado first will notice the mismatch; do not leave them to infer that the PSA covers it.

## Realized cost-uncertainty diagnostic

The six SSI cost tranches are sampled as **independent** gammas, so their weighted sum has a smaller coefficient of variation than any single tranche -- independence shrinks aggregate variance. This is how much cost uncertainty the PSA actually carries:

- **Realized CV of the total (weighted 24-month) cost per SSI: 0.1015** (mean $91,126, SD $9,246, 95% CrI $70,726 to $105,829, 2025 USD).
- Mean CV of a **single** tranche: 0.0799. Summed within type: deep total 0.0204, superficial total 0.0532 -- the shrinkage from independence.
- The Dirichlet split adds some of it back: CV of `frac_deep` = 0.1716, and deep and superficial SSI differ by roughly $61k per case, so the split is a material second source of cost spread.
- **For comparison, the uncertainty the PSA does NOT carry:** read on the same method-of-moments footing, `m_ssi_cost`'s DSA range implies a CV of **0.4630** on the *whole* cost block -- comparable to or larger than the 0.1015 the PSA does carry. Roughly half the defensible cost variance is outside the CEAC by design.

### A fourth disclosure, not mandated but material: the ciNPWT device price IS sampled

`c_device_cinpwt` is an **axis** elsewhere in this build (swept $100-$900 across the 161-point `SETTINGS['price_grid']` in `run_threshold.py` and Fig 3), and it is also `dist='gamma'` with a `derived_assumption` range of $100-$900. The contract's binding exclusions name only `p_base_ssi` and `m_ssi_cost`, and `run_log.d/inputs.md` objection 2 asks that the device price be excluded *"when [it is] being swept"* -- which it is not here, since the PSA sweeps `p` only. **It is therefore sampled -- truncated to the price axis -- and double-reported**, and the reader must know three things about that choice:

1. The $100-$900 span is an **assumed** spread on a parameter no source reports, not a measured CI. Read as a 95% CI it gives SE $204, i.e. a CV of 0.82 -- by far the widest relative spread in the sampled set, and wider than any evidence-derived parameter in the model.
2. **The fitted gamma ignored the price axis, so the draws are TRUNCATED to [$100, $900] by rejection resampling** (orchestrator decision 2026-08-09; the same idiom used for `du_sup` / `du_deep`, resampled rather than clipped so no point mass is created at either bound). Untruncated, the method-of-moments gamma is strongly right-skewed and does not respect the axis at all: median $195 against a mean of $249, realized range $0.31 to $2,023.05, with **24.80% of draws below the $100 floor and 1.36% above the $900 ceiling** of `SETTINGS['price_grid']`. A $0 and a $2,023 ciNPWT unit are outside the range this paper itself records as plausible -- wrong in both directions -- so they are not shipped. 3,535 draws were rejected and redrawn; the shipped column is asserted inside [$100, $900] before anything is written.
3. **The device price is represented TWICE in this build, and truncation does not fix that -- disclosure does.** It is sampled here *and* swept as analysis axis 2, where `run_threshold.py` reports a threshold price per stratum. So the CEAC propagates the same uncertainty a second time. At the **low stratum it is the dominant driver of CEAC width** (Spearman rho = -0.845, against -0.290 at the high stratum), which means P(cost-effective) at low risk is substantially a statement about a `derived_assumption` with no source rather than about clinical evidence. **Both numbers, so a reader can see exactly how much of the low-stratum width is device-price assumption:**

| P(CE) @ $100k, low stratum (p = 0.020) | value | mean INMB @ $100k (95% CrI) |
|---|---|---|
| **device price SAMPLED** (truncated $100-$900) | **0.7481** | $102 (-$352 to $387) |
| **device price HELD FIXED at $250** (every other parameter still sampled) | **0.9632** | $151 (-$15 to $318) |

   The difference -- 0.7481 against 0.9632 -- **is** the device-price assumption. Nearly all of the low stratum's residual doubt about ciNPWT comes from not knowing what the device costs, not from the clinical evidence. The **deterministic price axis (Fig 3, and the threshold price per stratum) is the honest presentation of that uncertainty**; the CEAC is the summary. Quote the low-stratum P(CE) with the device-price caveat attached, or quote the fixed-price figure and say the price is fixed.

**Where the six SSI cost tranches' dispersion now comes from.** Until the A2 audit these ranges were an ASSUMED `value x 0.5` to `value x 1.5` span, on the stated premise that 'Edmiston reports no SDs or CIs at all'. That premise was false. Edmiston's Table 3 is titled **'Mean SSI Cost (95% CI)'** and publishes a 95% confidence interval for **all twelve** payments, so the assumed span is retired. BUILD-CONTRACT section 9 still binds this module to read `[low, high]` as an approximate 95% CI with `SE = (high - low)/3.92`; what changed is that the bounds are now Edmiston's own. For the four 0-6-month tranches the cumulative payment IS the marginal one, so the published CI transfers verbatim. For the other eight the marginal SE is recovered as `sqrt(SE_t^2 - SE_(t-1)^2)` under an independent-increments assumption -- **declared here as an approximation**, because the two nested cumulative estimates are positively correlated and the covariance is not recoverable from the published table; the conservative alternative `SE_1 + SE_2` is reported as a check. The realized per-tranche CVs above are far below the retired assumption's 0.2551, ranging from about 0.02 (commercial deep, n = 210,019) to about 0.21 (Medicare superficial, n = 585), so the PSA is correspondingly tighter. Note what these intervals are and are not: they are Wald intervals on least-squares means from a log-link gamma GLM, i.e. SAMPLING precision on an adjusted mean, not the dispersion of cost across patients and not attribution uncertainty. Attribution uncertainty lives in `m_ssi_cost` and is handled deterministically.

## Verification performed at run time

- **Arm ordering: 0 inversions** in 610,000 draw x risk-point pairs (`n_ssi_B < n_ssi_A` in every one; smallest gap 2.781e-04). Guaranteed by construction: the engine applies `p_ciNPWT = p_control x RR` internally and the median-preserving lognormal keeps every RR draw below 1 (max drawn RR = 0.9442).
- **CEAC**: both probabilities asserted in [0,1] and summing to 1 at every one of the 81 WTP grid points, in each of the 3 strata.
- **Acceptability by risk**: monotonicity in `p` asserted at all three WTPs.
- **Truncation of `c_device_cinpwt`**: every shipped draw asserted inside [$100, $900] before writing -- realized $100.02 to $899.61, 0 below and 0 above.
- **Dominance labelling**: the vectorized classifier asserted identical to `model.incremental`'s own strings on all 10,000 intermediate-stratum draws.
- **Engine-read audit**: each candidate parameter was perturbed to its `high` bound one at a time and the engine's outputs watched, confirming that the 16 parameters declared engine-read are exactly the ones that move a result. Nothing inert was sampled into `psa_iterations.csv`.
